entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

2. The Petitioner is an accused in connection with T.R. Case No.15 of 2024 pending on the file of learned Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge under POCSO Act, Nabarangpur arising out of Kosagumuda P.S. Case No.52 of 2024 for commission of offence alleged under Sections 376(2)(n)/376(3)/323 of the IPC read with Section 6 of POCSO Act.
3. Learned counsel, on instruction, submits that except the present BLAPL, no other bail application of the Petitioner relating to the aforementioned P.S. case is pending in any other Court.

4. Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned Additional District & Sessions Judge-cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Nabarangpur by order dated 23.07.2023 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.
5. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioner is in custody since 03.03.2024.

6. It is further submitted that since victim in the meanwhile has been examined as P.W.20 and has been discharged, further continuance of the Petitioner in custody is not warranted, keeping in view the nature of allegation.

7. To fortify his submission, learned counsel for the Petitioner relies on the statement of the Doctor,
Iswar Rajgond vs State Of Odisha .... Opposite Party on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46241295/
1 P.W.10

entities.text: Iswar Rajgond vs State Of Odisha .... Opposite Party
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: and submits that the statement falsifies the claim of the Petitioner.
He also relies on the cross- examination of the victim regarding the relationship.
8. Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail.

9. It is trite law that this Court is not to make a microscopic examination of the evidence on record,
while considering the bail application.
10. Taking into account the nature of allegation and keeping in view the tenor of the statement of the victim-P.W.20, this Court is not inclined to entertain this bail application at this stage.
11. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
12. Liberty is granted to the Petitioner to renew his prayer before the learned Court in seisin at a later stage.
13. Since it is stated at the bar that the prosecution has cited 33 witnesses, learned Court in seisin is requested to conclude the trial with expediency as it deserves.
(V. NARASINGH) Judge Santoshi Designation: Senior Stenographer
